title: mixup: Beyond Empirical Risk Minimization
notes: A regularisation paper with an official repository (facebookresearch/mixup-cifar10) and CIFAR-10 experiments, so it is a good candidate for the official_repo path. The corrupted-label experiment is the most interesting claim: it is a large, clean effect that should survive shrinking.

claims.text: Training with mixup gives lower test error on CIFAR-10 than standard empirical risk minimisation with the same architecture.
claims.notes: The core comparison. Both arms are the same network, differing only in the data augmentation, which is the ideal shape for reduced-scale testing.

claims.text: Models trained with mixup memorise randomly corrupted labels less than models trained with standard ERM.
claims.notes: A large effect that appears even with heavy label noise on a small subset.

claims.text: Mixup improves robustness to adversarial examples relative to ERM.
claims.notes: Requires running an attack as well as training; at reduced scale the measurement is noisy.

claims.text: Mixup stabilises the training of generative adversarial networks.
claims.notes: GAN stability is hard to measure reliably and does not reduce cleanly to a single metric with a clear direction.

claims.text: A ResNet-50 trained with mixup reaches 22.1% top-1 error on ImageNet.
claims.notes: A headline number requiring ImageNet training.

claims.text: Larger values of the mixup interpolation strength alpha increase the difficulty of memorising corrupted labels.
claims.notes: A trend over alpha, testable with three or four values but noisy at small scale.

claims.text: Mixup outperforms ERM on the UCI tabular datasets.
claims.notes: Small datasets, so cheap to run, but the reported differences are small.
